Alex —

Appreciate the detailed sketch and the spreadsheet. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks so our pricing model matches your consumption geometry: 

Recap (what we heard)
- ~180M tokens/mo initial; 70% chat / 30% embeddings
- Avg tokens: chat ~450 (prompt+response), embeddings ~60
- Peak 99th TPS ~420, short bursts to ~600 for 1–3 minutes
- Target budget range $3.5k–$5k per 1M tokens

Clarifying questions (to pin unit economics):
1) What percent of chat calls are streaming vs non-streaming? Streaming affects latency SLO and throughput assumptions.
2) For chat completions, do you expect statefulness (long KV cache reuse across turns) or mostly stateless single-turn calls?
3) Any regional restrictions (traffic must stay us-east)?

Quick guidance from pricing POV (ballpark) — assuming hosted API, mixed traffic, and model family equivalent to a 7–13B LLM: 
- If you need 99th-slo at 420 TPS with sub-500ms tail, hosted tier with burst capability can work but unit price will be at the higher end of commercial bands (we'd expect an effective $/1M in the mid-to-high range versus our cheapest slab).
- If your pattern is sustained high concurrency (many sustained minutes at 400+ TPS), Dedicated reserved capacity can materially lower $/1M.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll spin up a short unit-econ sketch with two scenarios (hosted + burst vs dedicated) and include sensitivity to average tokens and streaming % (target delivery EOD tomorrow).
- Schedule a 30-min call with our pricing engineer (cc'd: Karthik) to review assumptions and run a quick costing model.

Are you available Tue 16 Mar 10:00–11:00 PT or 14:00–15:00 PT?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

- Burst behavior: Most days we’re quiet; roughly twice a week we see a marketing-triggered event that creates a 3–5 minute spike; those are the ~600 TPS bursts.
